policy: Full taxonomy coverage is an index, not a publishing queue. Pages may only be generated against evidence_tier T1-T3. T4 synthetic permutations are a hypothesis reserve consulted when a cluster has no evidence, and never publish on their own.

winnability_factor.measured_answer_engine_citation_occupanc: citation_occupancy = open_share of the citation slots an answer engine built its answer from, measured by scripts/queries/probe_query_class_occupancy.mjs. Preferred where present. That probe publishes the number ONLY while its known-open/known-closed control pair separates; while the controls do not separate it withholds citation_occupancy and no row here can carry this basis.
winnability_factor.keyword_tool_supplied_weak_incumbent_sco: weak_incumbent_score as supplied on the source row by a keyword tool. Used only where no citation occupancy has been measured.
winnability_factor.unmeasured_neutral: 1.0. No winnability evidence exists for this query, so ranking is not adjusted at all.
winnability_factor.replaced_placebo: weak_incumbent_score used to default to a hardcoded 0.5 on every row that lacked one - 64 of 68, including every measured T1 row. A constant factor changes no ordering and admits no page; it only made the file look as though winnability had been judged. It is gone: a row now carries a measurement, a supplied score, or an explicit neutral.
winnability_factor.publishing_gate: The neutral factor ranks but never admits. scripts/queries/join_atlas_to_release_queue.mjs requires winnability_basis = measured_answer_engine_citation_occupancy before a query can become a page candidate.

demand_value_by_band.measured_search_volume: search_volume (monthly searches from a keyword tool)
demand_value_by_band.own_impressions_only: impressions_90d (this domain's own impressions over 90 days)
demand_value_by_band.unscored: null - no demand evidence, rank_score is null

rank_scoring.comparability: rank_score is ONLY comparable within the same rank_band. The demand term carries a different unit per band, so a cross-band comparison is a unit error. Queries are ordered by band first, then by rank_score inside the band.
rank_scoring.why: Previously one field named `volume` held monthly search volume on semrush rows and this domain's own 90-day impressions on GSC rows, and rank_score was computed from it directly. That made a 40/mo keyword-tool query score off a single impression. Splitting the field and banding the score removes the comparison entirely.

unit_contract.search_volume: Monthly searches reported by a keyword tool. null when unknown.
unit_contract.impressions_90d: This domain's own impressions over the measured 90-day GSC window. null when unknown.
unit_contract.demand_basis: Which field rank_score used: search_volume | impressions_90d | none.
unit_contract.removed_field: `volume` is removed. It previously held BOTH monthly search volume (semrush rows) and this domain's own 90d impressions (gsc rows). A missing key throws; a wrong number does not.
unit_contract.never: Do not sum or compare across units. Disagreeing packet volumes are recorded in volume_sources with volume_conflict=true and are never averaged.
unit_contract.precedent: Follows portfolio_demand.json (portfolio-demand-v1), which separated volume_mo from demand_signal/demand_signal_unit for this same defect.
